abstract: The zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$ of OpenAI (2026), refined by Liu to $0.874957\ldots$ and Xu–Sang to $0.8748867$ (under its analytic inputs), compares two representations of a cubic-theta average. Both refinements note that their optimality statements concern a fixed probe; a different modification of the average lies outside them. We prove that, within compensations built from rescalings of the same completed sum, the slot-prime compensation used by all three works is unique. Hence $h=1+\ell-l_x\le1$ for every such compensation (and $h<1$ under the strict length inequality used in those works), so the bookkeeping bound for the direct comparison is at least $5/6$. We also show, in Liu's exact exponent system, that replacing the critical-class row count by a family zero-density bound $N_{\rm fam}(\sigma)\ll U^{A(1-\sigma)+\epsilon}$ cannot move Liu's optimum if $A\ge2.183363\ldots$ (uniformly over the moment parameter). It undercuts the critical count at Liu's optimal parameters iff $A<2.1807279\ldots$; the window between these is left open. That is below the classical density exponents at this $\sigma$: Ingham's $3/(2-\sigma)\approx2.298$ and Guth–Maynard's $30/13\approx2.308$. Numerical tables with positive controls accompany both statements. Finally, we prove a selection rule for which products of normalised Gauss sums carry the Möbius function modulo Hecke and ray characters. Within probes built from one Gauss-sum source and GL(1) Poisson duals, OAI's single sextic dual is the only $\mu$-carrying configuration with at most three duals, and quartic square-index coefficients admit none. No new zero-free region is claimed.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
Revision adding a new Section 5 and the reviewer's suggested algebraic monotonicity proof.
1. New Section 5 ("Which Gauss-sum products carry the Möbius function"). It replaces the v2 remark "the minimality of order 6 is heuristic" by a proved selection rule. Lemma G: modulo unitary Hecke characters and ray-class functions, a product of normalised N-th order Gauss sums at squarefree c is equivalent to mu^{E-1} g_K or mu^E, and it is equivalent to mu iff K + (N/2)(E+1) = 0 mod N. It assumes (W1), Weil's theorem that -J/sqrt(Np) is a Hecke character, and (W2), that the quadratic Gauss sum is a ray-class function. Lemma E (no hypothesis): mu, g_K and mu*g_K are not trivial in this quotient when 2K != 0. Proposition S gives the selection condition (5.2) for one source plus k GL(1) Poisson duals with optional quadratic twists. Corollaries: (i) for the cubic theta over Q(omega), unconditionally from [1, (4.7), Lemma 4.4], OAI's single twisted sextic dual is the only mu-carrying configuration with k <= 3, and the next ones have k = 4; (ii) an l-fold theta needs at least (l-1)/2 duals; (iii) for 4 | N with odd s (e.g. Suzuki's quartic square-index coefficients, as recorded in [4, (1.10)]) no probe in the class carries mu. A scope paragraph states the class restrictions and that no exponent bookkeeping is attempted. It also states that the scarce ingredient is a source with single-Gauss-sum coefficients, not the sign.
2. Proposition B(2): the grid check of the monotonicity of xi(kappa) is replaced by an algebraic proof. kappa'(xi) = 9(24xi^2-20xi+5)/(2(36xi^2-78xi+25)^2), the numerator has negative discriminant, and the denominator's roots 0.39111..., 1.7755... lie outside [xi(13/18), xi(1)].
3. Abstract: one sentence on Section 5. References [4]-[6] added (David-Dunn-Hamieh-Lin; Weil 1952; Ireland-Rosen).
4. Supplement: census/ (Hecke-multiplicativity test of -J for all 200 pairs at orders 3..10, 12; no exception) and grading_check.py (phase counts for the k=1 and k=4 configurations against non-mu controls).
Sections 1-4 are otherwise unchanged. No new zero-free region is claimed.
title: Structural ceilings in the cubic-theta quasi-Riemann-hypothesis argument
